q-105176.name: Question 1
q-105176.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2\le x<0,\,0<y\le 1\}.
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,\bbox[5px,border: 1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}},\,0<y<1\,\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
q-105176.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131516/assets/4f65a735e53130f633635fdfc8cd6de6c4fa39ed1fb7913ba9679bb07e73a6a0.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131516/assets/c76cea9b33420bf6c2e03d8eecb105003ce8b4e619063cbf2b7fccd5bc596cb2.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<x<0,\,0<y<1\,\}.
$$

q-161444.name: Question 2
q-161444.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ge 4\}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅$

II. $A-∂A=\text{int}\,A$

III. $∂A⊂A$
q-161444.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131516/assets/62c410c21e79e1bc688c1ff1a3440a207c62bcad42525bdc93fa2770b76d48bd.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131516/assets/33a4738b642443c2535d347aa53ee2b7b80c800142c4844d94578769118ebfbc.png)

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅,$ where $∅$ denotes the empty set.

- Statement II is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $A-∂A=\text{int}\,A.$

- Statement III is true. In this case, the set $A$ contains all of its boundary points, so we must have $∂A⊂A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

q-161601.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}<36\}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $A$ contains none of its boundary points.

II. $A$ contains some (not all) of its boundary points.

III. $\text{int}\,A=A$
q-161601.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131516/assets/ff1f735266f66879834e02ca7601e90e40dfa7929e5796d4a3f8cb4ff2828de7.png)

  

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

Notice that, in this case, the set $A$ contains none of its boundary points. 

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. As we've seen, $A$ contains none of its boundary points.

- Statement III is true. Since $A$ contains none of its boundary points, we must have $\text{int}\,A=A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

EXPLANATION

The boundary of a set A, denoted ∂A, is the set that contains all the boundary points of A.

The set A and its boundary ∂A are shown below.

The interior of a set A, denoted intA, is the set containing all the interior points of A. It contains every point in A except the boundary points: intA=A−∂A

The interior of A is shown below.

So, in this case, the interior of A is given by
